newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBS END STRONGER IN TOKYO BUT OFF EARLIER HIGHS.
newsitem.headline: JGBS END STRONGER IN TOKYO BUT OFF EARLIER HIGHS.

text.p: The benchmark September 10-year Japanese government bond (JGB) futures contract ended Friday trade firmer but off earlier highs hit after the release of key data sparked a brief buying spree, traders said.

An announcement that June machinery orders had fallen 10.6 percent month-on-month set off an immediate surge that took key September up to 126.81. But then selling ensued on forecasts that the July-September quarter will see a rise in machinery orders of 2.2 percent, with loss-cut sales also emerging.
September finished at 126.63, up 0.13 from Thursday's close, after ranging from 126.51 to 126.81.

"The approaching weekend, and the fact that many operators will be on vacation next week, makes people extremely wary of holding positions. A number of people who bought in haste after the June figures came out sold soon after when the contract failed to rise, partly for this reason," one trader said.
But the downside was expected to be solidly supported by buying on dips from investors and others, he added.
Light buying at the longer end from public funds was detected, as it has been for several days, and this was offering additional support, one city bank trader said.
Traders said the machinery orders figures were unlikely to have much lasting impact, adding that trade next week is expected to be fairly quiet in the absence of economic indicators until Friday.

One trust bank trader said he expected the key September contract to consolidate between 126.00 and 127.00, but that wariness about whether it had recently been overbought was expected to limit gains.
"There are currently few to no selling factors, not to mention that the market has become strangely unresponsive to these anyway. Expect range-bound trade," another said.
One securities firm trader said there was a slim chance that the benchmark cash JGB could set a new record low yield next week. The 182nd 10-year cash bond hit 2.070 percent this past Monday.
The yield on the key cash bonds stood at 2.105 percent at 0641 GMT against 2.115 on Thursday, after moving from 2.085 to 2.105 percent.

But this hinges partly on a futures' rise to over 127.00, which may require fresh factors, such as another rally in U.S. Treasuries, because those who built longs earlier this week are waiting to take profits, traders said.
